source.title: Rank stability in quadratic extensions and Hilbert's tenth problem for the ring of integers of a number field
source.authors: Levent Alpöge, Manjul Bhargava, Wei Ho and Ari Shnidman
source.venue: Inventiones mathematicae 243 (2026), no. 3, 1129–1139; online 1 December 2025. The downloaded publisher PDF header itself says (2025); the journal landing page assigns volume 243 to 2026.
readSections: The whole published version (11 pages: abstract, §§1–4, references), read 2026-09-22. PDF https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-025-01392-3.pdf (CC BY 4.0), SHA-256 94190b392b135905918368a0f52bb0ec1491488f65d9228fdabcee0bf08281ec. Locators are its printed pages.

The whole of arXiv v1 (30 January 2025, 10 pages), read 2026-09-22 from its TeX source mainv2.tex. PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.18774v1, SHA-256 3d36dff3653d7484c240f36484ddaff8c90bd8bb94c510113723a2538b859d5a; source tarball SHA-256 ca6f068988c7df2e188007c3d1911f14a8894d593cc6605f1d6acc280b78f40f. v1 and the published version were compared line by line. The published version corrects the cover π in Proposition 2.7 and the Fermat curve in the introduction (E1, E2). It replaces the proof of Lemma 2.6 by a Northcott argument, strengthens Corollary 1.2 from 'diophantine model' to 'ℤ is Diophantine over 𝒪_K', and adds the Diophantine-set definition, Denef–Lipshitz's conjecture and the Eisenträger consequence to §1. The theorem numbering is the same in both.

Inputs read where the paper relies on them: Yu, J. Number Theory 160 (2016), arXiv:1511.07511v1 (Theorem 4 = Theorem 4.13, §§1–4); Mazur–Rubin–Shlapentokh, J. Number Theory 254 (2024), arXiv:2208.09963v3 (Definition 2.2, Proposition 2.3, Theorems 3.1 and 4.8, Lemmas 4.3–4.7); Kai, arXiv:2306.16983v5 (Theorem 13.1, statement only).

Independent review, Codex codex-hjdg0j, 2026-09-23: all eleven pages of the published article; comparison with arXiv v1 at the changed introduction, Lemma 2.6 and Proposition 2.7 and the six finding locators. The author-hosted nine-page preprint was checked at §§2.4–4 through the public web reader; it still has the old cover and circle-method formulas. Its direct download returned HTTP 403, so no byte hash is claimed.

Independent prerequisite checks: Yu v1 Theorem 4, Proposition 4.2 and proof, §4 setup, Proposition 4.12 proof and Theorem 4.13; MRS v3 Definition 2.2, Proposition 2.3(1), Theorem 3.1, Lemma 4.1 (p. 9) and Lemmas 4.2–4.7, Theorem 4.8 and proof; Kai v5 Theorem 13.1, pp. 56–57. These are statement/application checks, not a claim to have independently read all proofs in those three papers.

summary: The paper proves positive rank stability for every quadratic number-field extension and deduces Diophantine definability of Z, hence undecidability, over every ring of integers. Independent review preserves these targets, corrects library and statement overclaims, adds the missing logical reductions and the explicit Kai-to-prime-triples argument, and confirms six original source findings plus one affine-coset misprint. The dyadic rescaling is valid for choosing the main theorem’s r but does not prove Proposition 2.5 for its original r. Mitsui’s exact analytic input and Eisenträger’s Chapter 7 proof also remain explicit gaps. Three source routes are accepted; routes 2 and 5 require revision. No result is claimed formalised.

items.name: Diophantine subsets of a ring; O_F Diophantine in O_K
items.statement: For a commutative ring R with identity and k ≥ 0, a subset E ⊆ R^k is Diophantine if finitely many polynomials f_i ∈ R[t_1,…,t_k,x_1,…,x_n] satisfy t ∈ E iff there exists x ∈ R^n with every f_i(t,x)=0. For F ⊆ K number fields this applies to the image of O_F in O_K. Reduction to one polynomial is a separate theorem (item 45).
items.locator: §1, p. 1130 (published version); the systems form is MRS, Definition 2.2
items.note: Mathlib's `Dioph` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Dioph.lean) defines Diophantine subsets of ℕ^α only, with integer polynomials. Neither library has Diophantine subsets of an arbitrary ring, nor the reduction from systems to one equation. The arXiv v1 introduction does not define the notion. It is added in the published version.

items.name: Hilbert's tenth problem over ℤ (Davis–Putnam–Robinson, Matiyasevich)
items.statement: Every recursively enumerable subset of ℕ^k is Diophantine over ℤ. Consequently there is no algorithm that decides, for f ∈ ℤ[x_1, …, x_n], whether f has a zero in ℤ^n.
items.note: LD.4 plans the negative solution over ℤ through a complete MRDP source chain. Mathlib has the key exponential step: `Dioph.pow_dioph` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Dioph.lean) shows that exponentiation is Diophantine, and the file's TODO records that the solution of Hilbert's tenth problem is unfinished.

items.name: Transfer of undecidability along Diophantine definitions
items.statement: If a commutative ring R contains Z and the image of Z is Diophantine in R, solvability of finite polynomial systems over R is undecidable: substitute the fixed defining system for every variable of an integer polynomial. Coefficients are given by finite expressions in a fixed presentation; only finitely many constants of R are needed for this reduction. For rings of integers, combine this with item 45 to obtain undecidability for a single equation. Transitivity and finite-extension descent are separately items 46 and 48.
items.locator: §1, p. 1130; MRS Proposition 2.3(1) and Lemma 4.3
items.note: This is the interpretation step that LD.4's acceptance criterion asks for: undecidability over ℤ is not copied to other rings without its own interpretation theorem. It is absent from both libraries.

items.name: Diophantine definitions from rank stability (Poonen, Cornelissen–Pheidas–Zahidi, Shlapentokh; Mazur–Rubin–Shlapentokh Theorem 3.1)
items.statement: Let K/F be an extension of number fields and A/F an abelian variety with rank A(K) = rank A(F) ≥ 1. Then 𝒪_F has a Diophantine definition over 𝒪_K. The elliptic-curve case with rank E(F) = rank E(K) = 1 is due to Poonen and to Cornelissen–Pheidas–Zahidi, and the case rank E(F) = rank E(K) > 0 to Poonen and Shlapentokh.
items.locator: §1, p. 1130, citing [23], [1], [27] and [16, Theorem 3.1]; MRS Theorem 3.1 (proved in MRS Proposition 14.3 and Lemma 13.8)
items.note: This is an input the paper cites, not a result it proves. Its proof uses divisibility of denominators of multiples of a point on A, norm equations and Denef's non-zero lemma (MRS Lemma 4.6). None of this is planned: LD.4 covers MRDP over ℤ only.

items.name: ℤ is Diophantine over the ring of integers of a totally real field (Denef)
items.statement: If M is a totally real number field, then ℤ is Diophantine over 𝒪_M. Denef–Lipshitz extend this to quadratic extensions of totally real fields.
items.locator: §1, p. 1130, citing Denef [3, 4] and Denef–Lipshitz [5]; used in the proof of MRS Theorem 4.8
items.note: This is an input of item 6, and the classical base case of the theory (Denef 1980, via Pell equations over totally real fields). It is absent from both libraries and from the atlas.

items.name: Quadratic rank stability everywhere implies ℤ Diophantine over every 𝒪_K (Shlapentokh; MRS Theorem 4.8)
items.statement: Suppose that for every quadratic extension of number fields K/F, 𝒪_F has a Diophantine definition over 𝒪_K. Then ℤ has a Diophantine definition over the ring of integers of every number field. In particular, the conclusion holds if every quadratic K/F admits an abelian variety A/F with rank A(F) = rank A(K) > 0, by item 4. Proof: reduce to M/ℚ Galois. Each complex conjugation σ gives a quadratic extension M/M^σ, so 𝒪_{M^σ} is Diophantine in 𝒪_M. Intersect over σ to get 𝒪_{M^+} for the totally real field M^+ = ∩M^σ, then apply Denef (item 5) and transitivity (item 3). If M is totally real, use Denef directly: its complex conjugations are identities, not generators of quadratic extensions. Descent from the Galois closure to the original field uses the finite-extension clause of MRS Lemma 4.3 (item 48), not transitivity alone.
items.locator: §1, p. 1130, citing [16, Theorems 3.1 and 4.8]; MRS Theorem 4.8, p. 10–11
items.note: This is the reduction the paper's Corollary 1.2 rests on. It is absent from both libraries and the atlas.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (rank stability in quadratic extensions)
items.statement: For every quadratic extension K/F of number fields there is an abelian variety A/F with rank A(F)=rank A(K)>0. More precisely, set F′=F(ζ_ell), K′=K(ζ_ell), for an odd prime ell not dividing the absolute discriminant of K. Over F′ construct the positive-rank Jacobian of y²=x^ell+r²a^(ell−1)b² whose K′/F′-twist has rank zero, and restrict scalars from F′ to the original F. The dyadic rescaling in E3 is made before choosing a,b.
items.note: The paper's main theorem. §4 (item 43) proves it from items 11–13, 18, 23, 25, 27 and 31.

items.name: Corollary 1.2 (Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers)
items.statement: Let K be any number field. Then ℤ is Diophantine over 𝒪_K, and so Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative answer over 𝒪_K: there is no algorithm that decides whether a polynomial equation in several variables over 𝒪_K has solutions in 𝒪_K.
items.locator: Corollary 1.2, p. 1130 (published version). arXiv v1 states the weaker 'ℤ has a diophantine model over 𝒪_K'
items.note: This follows from Theorem 1.1 and items 4, 6 and 3. The published statement (a Diophantine definition of ℤ) is what the MRS results give. The v1 wording ('diophantine model') is weaker, so it is not a mistake.

items.name: Hilbert's tenth problem over finitely generated infinite ℤ-algebras (Eisenträger)
items.statement: Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative answer over every finitely generated infinite ℤ-algebra. This follows from Corollary 1.2 and Eisenträger's thesis, Chapter 7.
items.locator: §1, p. 1130 (published version only), citing [6, Chap. 7]
items.note: Stated in the published introduction, not proved there. The exact Chapter 7 reduction has not been acquired independently: G2 records the missing proof and the required treatment of positive characteristic and zero divisors. Do not infer this from Diophantine definability of Z alone, which cannot hold inside a positive-characteristic ring.

items.name: Mordell–Weil theorem and rank of an abelian variety over a number field
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field F, A(F) is a finitely generated abelian group. rank A(F) denotes its rank.
items.locator: used throughout; §1, §4
items.note: RP.1 plans weak Mordell–Weil and finite generation for abelian varieties. Tau Ceti proves Mordell–Weil for elliptic curves only, and its audit marks the abelian-variety case absent.

items.name: Cyclotomic disjointness from coprime discriminants
items.statement: For number fields K and Q(ζ_ell) in a common overfield, ell an odd prime not dividing Disc(K), K and Q(ζ_ell) are linearly disjoint over Q. Apply the coprime-discriminant theorem with the cyclotomic field as the Galois argument and Disc(Q(ζ_ell))=(−1)^((ell−1)/2)ell^(ell−2).
items.note: The three pinned declarations were read in their source files. They establish disjointness (and the equivalent intersection statement), not all the original bundled base-change conclusions. Those are separated into application item 53.

items.name: Weil restriction reduction
items.statement: Let F' = F(ζ_ℓ) and K' = K(ζ_ℓ), with K and F(ζ_ℓ) linearly disjoint over F. If A/F' is an abelian variety with rank A(F') = rank A(K') > 0, then A' := Res_{F'/F} A is an abelian variety over F with A'(F) = A(F') and A'(K) = A(F' ⊗_F K) = A(K'). So rank A'(F) = rank A'(K) > 0.
items.note: A6 plans Weil restriction of abelian schemes along finite étale maps, and that it is again an abelian scheme. The point identity A'(T) = A(T ⊗_F F') is its functor-of-points definition.

api.statement: For a finite separable F′/F and F-algebra T, points of Res A over T identify functorially with A(T tensor_F F′).

api.statement: Over K linearly disjoint from F′, the tensor algebra is K F′, not a product of fields.

api.statement: Transport of the point-group equivalences identifies the two ranks used in the reduction.

items.name: Rank of an abelian variety over a quadratic extension
items.statement: Let A/F be an abelian variety, K/F quadratic, and A^K the quadratic twist of A by the character of K/F. Then rank A(K) = rank A(F) + rank A^K(F). The geometric construction behind this identity is that Res_{K/F}(A_K) is isogenous to A × A^K, and A(K) ⊗ ℚ splits into the ± eigenspaces of Gal(K/F), identified with A(F) ⊗ ℚ and A^K(F) ⊗ ℚ.
items.note: This is used with A = J_{r²t²} and A^K = J_{q^ℓr²t²}. Only the elliptic case over ℚ is planned, at RankZeroOneBSD BSD.1 (Tau Ceti has the eigenspace identifications `quadraticTwistPointEquiv` but not the rank identity). Quadratic twists of abelian varieties are not planned anywhere.

items.name: The curves C_n : y² = x^ℓ + n and their Jacobians with ℤ[ζ]-multiplication
items.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime, F a number field containing μ_ℓ, and ζ a generator of μ_ℓ. For n ∈ F^×, C_n is the smooth projective model of the affine hyperelliptic curve y² = x^ℓ + n. It has genus (ℓ − 1)/2 and a unique point ∞ at infinity. C_n ≅ C_{nλ^{2ℓ}} for λ ∈ F^×, via (x, y) ↦ (λ²x, λ^ℓy). The automorphism (x, y) ↦ (ζx, y) gives an action of μ_ℓ on C_n, and hence an embedding ℤ[ζ] ↪ End(J_n) for J_n := Jac(C_n).
items.note: The Jacobian of a pointed curve and its functoriality are planned by the Jacobian Challenge (Layers D–F), and hyperelliptic function fields by Algebraic Curves Layer 10. The family, its μ_ℓ-action and the resulting CM by ℤ[ζ] are not planned. Neither library has hyperelliptic or superelliptic curves (a name search finds none).

items.name: Quadratic twists and μ_ℓ-twists of C_n and J_n
items.statement: For K=F(√q), the quadratic twist q y²=x^ell+n is F-isomorphic to C_(q^ell n) via (x,y)↦(q x,q^((ell+1)/2)y), and Jacobians have the corresponding twist isomorphism. If alpha^ell=t, an isomorphism C_(nt²)→C_n is (x,y)↦(x/alpha²,y/t). Pin the coordinate action rho(ζ)(x,y)=(ζx,y), and its pushforward action on the Jacobian. For chi_t(sigma)=sigma(alpha²)/alpha², transporting the new curve’s Galois action to J_n gives rho(chi_t(sigma)) composed with the old action. Equivalently, images of F-rational points satisfy sigma(P)=rho(chi_t(sigma)^(-1))P. Using pullback instead of pushforward reverses the character convention. Classes t modulo F^{×ell} parameterize these mu_ell-twists.
items.locator: §2, p. 1132; proof of Lemma 2.6 (arXiv v1, p. 5; the published proof uses the same twisting)
items.note: The old unqualified tensor-character formula hid the variance of the induced Jacobian action. The explicit coordinate map now fixes it; no source error is asserted from this convention choice. The pinned TauCeti.kummerClassMap is injective, not a proved Kummer isomorphism or a classification of curve twists. The missing geometric descent is not supplied by this near miss.

items.name: The kernel of φ = 1 − ζ
items.statement: φ = 1 − ζ is an isogeny J_n → J_n of degree ℓ. J_n[φ](F̄) is a one-dimensional 𝔽_ℓ-vector space spanned by the nonzero class (0, √n) − ∞, which is fixed by ζ. G_F acts on it through the quadratic character of F(√n)/F. In particular J_n[φ] is isomorphic to its Cartier dual, since μ_ℓ ⊂ F.
items.note: TauCeti.Isogeny.degree takes WeierstrassCurve.Affine arguments: it is elliptic-only. The old claim that this declaration gives degrees of isogenies of arbitrary abelian varieties was false. Import general finite-isogeny degree theory from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3/A6, then compute this particular kernel. Fix the induced-action convention as in item 15.
items.proofOutline: On C_n, div(y−sqrt(n))=ell·((0,sqrt(n))−infinity). The class is nonzero by the genus≥1 Abel-map argument, so it has order ell. The cyclotomic action obeys [ell]=u(1−ζ)^(ell−1) for a unit u. Since dim J_n=(ell−1)/2 and deg[ell]=ell^(ell−1), multiplicativity of finite-isogeny degree gives deg(1−ζ)=ell. Thus the exhibited subgroup exhausts the geometric kernel. The hyperelliptic involution identifies the two points over x=0 with opposite divisor classes, giving the quadratic character. Cartier self-duality follows because this character is its inverse and mu_ell⊂F.

items.name: The φ-Selmer group Sel_φ(J_n)
items.statement: Set T = H¹(F, J_n[φ]) and T_𝔭 = H¹(F_𝔭, J_n[φ]). Let W_𝔭 ⊆ T_𝔭 be the image of the connecting map J_n(F_𝔭) → T_𝔭 of 0 → J_n[φ] → J_n → J_n → 0. Then Sel_φ(J_n) = ker(T → ∏_𝔭 T_𝔭/W_𝔭), the product over finite primes. Archimedean places are ignored because F ⊇ μ_ℓ is totally complex.
items.note: RP.1 plans Kummer maps and finite Selmer groups for isogenies of abelian varieties. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7 plans Selmer structures and Selmer groups for a general discrete Galois module. The libraries have only the elliptic 2-descent Selmer group in square-class form.

items.name: Lemma 2.1 (Selmer bound for φ = 1 − ζ)
items.statement: J_n(F)/φJ_n(F) ↪ Sel_φ(J_n), so rank_{ℤ[ζ]} J_n(F) ≤ dim_{𝔽_ℓ} Sel_φ(J_n). In particular, Sel_φ(J_n) = 0 implies rank J_n(F) = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 2.1, p. 1132
items.note: The Kummer injection is RP.1's. The ℤ[ζ]-rank inequality is not: J_n(F) is a finitely generated module over the Dedekind domain ℤ[ζ], and (1 − ζ) is a prime of residue field 𝔽_ℓ. The ordinary Z-rank is (ell−1) times the Z[ζ]-rank. The inequality follows by localizing the torsion-free part at the prime (1−ζ), where it is free of that rank; the torsion contribution to M/(1−ζ)M can only increase its dimension.

items.name: Local Tate duality and the local Euler characteristic formula for finite modules
items.statement: For a finite G_{F_𝔭}-module M with 𝔭 ∤ #M: H²(F_𝔭, M) is dual to H⁰(F_𝔭, M^∨(1)), and #H¹(F_𝔭, M) = #H⁰(F_𝔭, M) · #H²(F_𝔭, M).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.2, p. 1133, citing Tate [29]
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans `tateDualityPairing_perfect_mixed`, finiteness `finite_H` and the cardinality Euler characteristic.

items.name: Lemma 2.2 (silent primes)
items.statement: Call 𝔭 silent if T_𝔭 = 0. If 𝔭 ∤ ℓ is inert or ramified in F(√n)/F, then T_𝔭 = H¹(F_𝔭, J_n[φ]) = 0: local duality gives #H² = #H⁰, and the Euler characteristic gives #T_𝔭 = (#J_n[φ](F_𝔭))² = 1 because √n ∉ F_𝔭. Silent primes exist if and only if n is not a square in F.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2 and the remark after it, p. 1133
items.note: This applies item 19 to the module of item 16. The terminology is Mazur–Rubin's (Diophantine stability, 2018). The existence remark uses Chebotarev for F(√n)/F (item 37).

items.name: Local conditions at good primes
items.statement: For a finite place p of F of residue characteristic different from ell, an abelian variety A/F_p with good reduction and an isogeny phi:A→B of degree ell, its Kummer image B(F_p)/phi A(F_p) in H¹(F_p,A[phi]) equals the unramified subgroup. The latter is the kernel of restriction to inertia, equivalently H¹(Gal(F_p^un/F_p),A[phi]) because good reduction and prime-to-residue-characteristic degree make A[phi] unramified. In the paper B=A=J_n.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.4, p. 1134
items.note: RP.1's finite Selmer groups for isogenies need exactly this. The unramified-versus-bad-prime comparison is also named in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1, and the elliptic case in Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7.

items.name: Good reduction is preserved by twists unramified at 𝔭
items.statement: If 𝔭 ∤ ℓ, J_{q^ℓr²} has good reduction at 𝔭, and t is a 𝔭-unit, then J_{q^ℓr²t²} also has good reduction at 𝔭, because the twisting cocycle χ_t is unramified at 𝔭. The proof is Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.4, p. 1134
items.note: R11.5 plans the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion for abelian varieties.

items.name: Lemma 2.3 (Yu's theorem: a μ_ℓ-twist with trivial φ-Selmer group)
items.statement: Let K = F(√q) be a quadratic extension, unramified at the primes above ℓ. There is nonzero r ∈ 𝒪_F with Sel_φ(J_{q^ℓr²}) = 0, and r may be taken outside every prime that ramifies in K. This is Yu, J. Number Theory 160 (2016), Theorem 4 (= Theorem 4.13): if K ∋ ζ_p, f ∈ K[x] is separable of degree n with p ∤ n an odd prime and Gal(f) ≅ S_n, then for every r ≥ 0 there are infinitely many p-twists C_{p,df} (d ∈ K^×/K^{×p}) of y^p = f(x) with dim_{𝔽_p} Sel_π(J(C_{p,df})/K) = r. It is applied with p = ℓ and f(y) = y² − q^ℓ, since C_{q^ℓr²} is x^ℓ = r²((y/r)² − q^ℓ), and Gal(f) ≅ S_2 exactly when q is not a square.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3, p. 1133; Yu, Theorem 4 (p. 3) and Theorem 4.13 (arXiv:1511.07511)
items.note: The argument is Mazur–Rubin twisting: a prime at which the local conditions of J and its twist differ changes the Selmer rank by one (Yu §§2–4). The second sentence ('clear from his proof') checks out against Yu's proof. The rank-lowering twist (Proposition 4.2) uses d ≡ 1 modulo a modulus θ containing every bad prime of J_{q^ℓ}, including every prime ramified in K. The rank-raising twist (Proposition 4.12) is trivial at a set Σ(ℓ) containing them. So every twist is by an element that is a unit at the ramified primes, and r can be chosen prime to them. Only rank lowering is needed: iterate Proposition 4.2. Every twisting element is congruent to 1 at the chosen bad primes. Since 2 is invertible modulo ell, each resulting class d is represented by r²: choose r=d^((ell+1)/2) modulo ell-th powers and clear denominators by ell-th powers away from the protected primes. The ramified primes of K/F are bad for J_(q^ell), since the phi-torsion character is ramified there (they do not divide ell); thus the protected set includes them.

items.name: The prime sets S′, S, S_inert, Σ and the Σ-units
items.statement: S′ is the set of primes dividing ℓ! or the conductor of J_{q^ℓr²}. S ⊆ S′ is the set of 𝔭 ∈ S′ that lie above ℓ or split in K/F. S_inert is the infinite set of primes inert in K. Σ = S ∪ S_inert. 𝒪_{F,Σ}^× = {x ∈ F^× : x ∈ 𝒪_{F,𝔭}^× for every 𝔭 ∉ Σ}. In particular all primes above ell lie in S whether split or inert; S contains no ramified prime of K/F. Reuse the existing Set.unit carrier for the arbitrary infinite set Sigma (item 57), rather than defining a second S-unit group.
items.note: The group of units away from an arbitrary (even infinite) set of primes is Mathlib's `Set.unit` (Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger.lean). The specific sets S′, S and Σ are the paper's.

items.name: Lemma 2.4 (silent twists preserve the Selmer group)
items.statement: Let t ∈ 𝒪_{F,Σ}^× with t ∈ F_𝔭^{×ℓ} for all 𝔭 ∈ S. Then Sel_φ(J_{q^ℓr²t²}) = Sel_φ(J_{q^ℓr²}) = 0, as subgroups of the common ambient space T = H¹(F, J_{q^ℓ}[φ]). The proof compares local conditions. For 𝔭 ∈ S the two curves are isomorphic over F_𝔭. For 𝔭 inert or ramified in K, T_𝔭 = 0 by Lemma 2.2. Otherwise 𝔭 ∤ ℓ and both Jacobians have good reduction, so W_𝔭 = H¹_un for both.
items.note: Uses items 20–22. The identification J_{q^ℓr²t²}[φ] ≅ J_{q^ℓ}[φ] is defined only up to a scalar in 𝔽_ℓ^×, which does not change the subspaces W_𝔭. The coefficient identifications and isomorphisms must commute with the local connecting maps, so compare subspaces under the same chosen identification; an abstract isomorphism of Jacobians alone is insufficient.

items.name: The classes t_{a,b} and the set X
items.statement: For a, b ∈ F^×, t_{a,b} ∈ F^×/F^{×ℓ} is the class of a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b. X is the set of t_{a,b} with a, b ∈ 𝒪_{F,Σ}^×, (i) 1 = a + 2rb, and (ii) a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b ∈ F_𝔭^{×ℓ} for all 𝔭 ∈ S. Condition (i) serves Proposition 2.7 and (ii) serves Lemma 2.4.
items.note: The published version lists conditions (i) and (ii) explicitly. arXiv v1 has only the set-builder definition.

items.name: Proposition 2.5 (infinitely many admissible Σ-unit solutions)
items.statement: With F, K=F(√q), ell, the fixed nonzero r of Lemma 2.3 and S,Sigma of §2.3, the set X of admissible classes in item 26 is infinite. This is the published Proposition 2.5, with its fixed-r proof obligation G3 retained.
items.locator: Proposition 2.5, p. 1134; proof in §3, pp. 1136–1137
items.note: Published target retained verbatim: X for the fixed r of §2.3 is infinite. The dyadic rescaling repair in E3 proves the variant needed for the existential main theorem after choosing r anew. It does not, without further argument, prove this target for the original r, since delta is supported outside Sigma. This is explicit proof gap G3. The non-proportional count and exceptional-family removal needed for E6 are item 52.
items.proofOutline: Proof (§3): let 𝔪 be the conductor of K/F and ψ : Cl_F(𝔪) → ℤ/2 the character of K/F. Choose γ ∈ 𝒪_F with γ ∈ 𝔭 exactly for 𝔭 ∈ S, and apply Proposition 3.1 with β = 2rγ^{nℓ}, n large. If 𝔪 = 1, take I a prime ideal with [I] ∉ ker ψ, so that every I-prime is an S_inert-unit. If 𝔪 ≠ 1, take I = 𝒪_F and prescribe the p_i modulo 𝔪 so that they are inert in K. In both cases impose p_2 ≡ p_3 (mod 𝔭^n) for 𝔭 ∈ S, and set a = p_1/p_3 and b = γ^{nℓ}p_2/p_3. Then a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b = (1 − 2rb)^{(ℓ−1)/2}γ^{nℓ}p_2/p_3 is an ℓ-th power at every 𝔭 ∈ S. Infinitude: the ideals (p_1^{(ℓ−1)/2}p_2p_3^{(ℓ−1)/2}) have infinite support, by Siegel–Mahler, and their large primes occur with multiplicity < ℓ.

items.name: Northcott finiteness for points of height zero and bounded degree on an abelian variety
items.statement: Fix an abelian variety A/F, a symmetric ample line bundle L on A and its absolute Neron–Tate height hhat_L. For D≥1, there are finitely many P∈A(Fbar) with [F(P):F]≤D and hhat_L(P)=0; these are exactly the torsion points of degree at most D. Ampleness is essential (the zero height from a trivial bundle does not have this property).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.6, p. 1134 (published version)
items.note: RP.0 plans the height machine with Northcott and Néron–Tate heights on abelian varieties. Tau Ceti has the canonical height of an elliptic curve only (`WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight`). arXiv v1 argued instead through potentially good reduction of CM abelian varieties (Serre–Tate §5) and the Weil bound over a totally ramified extension.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 (only finitely many twists acquire extra torsion)
items.statement: Let n ∈ F^×. There are only finitely many t ∈ F^×/F^{×ℓ} with J_{nt²}(F)_tors ≠ J_{nt²}[φ](F). Proof (published): a torsion point of J_{nt²}(F) is a point of J_n(F̄) of height 0 and degree ≤ ℓ, and there are finitely many by Northcott. Suppose s/t is not an ℓ-th power, and torsion points of J_{nt²}(F) and J_{ns²}(F) give the same P ∈ J_n(F̄). The two twisted Galois actions differ by a nontrivial power of ζ, so P is fixed by ζ and lies in J_n[1 − ζ].
items.locator: Lemma 2.6, p. 1134. arXiv v1, p. 5, has a different proof: a uniform torsion bound from potentially good reduction of CM abelian varieties and Weil bounds, then the characters χ_t
items.note: The published proof uses item 28 on the fixed J_n, so there is no need for a family-uniform height estimate. Choose the isomorphisms through alpha^ell=t as in item 15. Two distinct twist characters differ nontrivially; a shared point is fixed by a nontrivial power of ζ, hence by ζ. The earlier CM-reduction proof is not used in the revised dependency graph; no independent certification of all its local reduction inputs is claimed.

items.name: The twisted Fermat curve and its cover of C_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}
items.statement: Over ℚ̄, C_n is a μ_ℓ-quotient of the Fermat curve x^ℓ + y^ℓ = z^ℓ (McCallum). For a, b with a + 2rb = 1, let C̃ : ax^ℓ + 2rby^ℓ = z^ℓ. On the open subset z = 1, y ≠ 0, the map π(x, y) = (axy^{−2}, a^{(ℓ−1)/2}(y^{−ℓ} − rb)) sends C̃ to C_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}, and π(1, 1) = P = (a, a^{(ℓ−1)/2}(1 − rb)) ∈ C_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F). Extend the rational map uniquely to the smooth projective curves by properness of the target. The formula is not a regular coordinate formula at y=0.
items.locator: before and in the proof of Proposition 2.7, pp. 1134–1135 (published); introduction, p. 1131
items.note: Checked symbolically for ℓ = 3, 5, 7: on C̃, (axy^{−2})^ℓ + r²a^{ℓ−1}b² = a^{ℓ−1}(y^{−ℓ} − rb)². arXiv v1 prints axy^{−1}, which does not map C̃ to the curve (sourceIssue E1). The v1 introduction names the wrong Fermat curve (E2). The published version corrects both.

items.statement: For all but finitely many t_(a,b)∈X, J_(r²a^(ell−1)b²) has positive rank over F. For these twists Lemma 2.6 identifies rational torsion with the rational phi-kernel. The point P=(a,a^((ell−1)/2)(1−rb)) has a≠0, so its Abel–Jacobi class is outside that kernel by item 54 and therefore has infinite order.

items.name: I-primes
items.statement: For a nonzero integral ideal I of O_F, an element p∈I is an I-prime if |Norm_(F/Q)(p)|/Norm(I) is a rational prime. Equivalently (p)I^(-1) is a prime ideal of residue degree one. The nonzero-ideal hypothesis makes the norm quotient defined.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1136; statement of Proposition 3.1, p. 1135
items.note: This definition belongs to Proposition 3.1 and is routed with it.

items.name: Mitsui's generalized prime number theorem (Siegel–Walfisz over number fields)
items.statement: Prime elements, and prime ideals, of a number field F are equidistributed in ray classes, and in residue classes modulo C, uniformly for moduli up to a power of log of the height, with a Siegel–Walfisz error term. This is the major-arc input for Proposition 3.1.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 1136, citing Mitsui [18] (Jpn. J. Math. 26 (1956))
items.note: Neither library has Hecke L-functions or a prime ideal theorem in progressions (the AN.4 audit lists Hecke characters as absent). Chebotarev, planned by Tau Ceti, gives densities without uniformity in the modulus. Independent review: this is only a description of an input, not an exact theorem with its angular region, archimedean normalization, modulus range and error. G1 prevents acceptance of route 2 until a precise public primary-source statement is acquired. The Kai route to item 34 does not consume item 33.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (three primes in a linear equation over a number field, with congruences)
items.statement: Let F be a totally complex number field, I ⊆ 𝒪_F a nonzero integral ideal, C ∈ ℤ^+ prime to I, β ∈ 2𝒪_F nonzero, and u_1, u_2, u_3 ∈ (𝒪_F/(C))^× with u_1 + βu_2 ≡ u_3 (mod C). Then there are infinitely many triples (p_1, p_2, p_3), modulo 𝒪_F^×, with each p_i an I-prime, p_1 + βp_2 = p_3, and p_i ≡ u_i (mod C).
items.locator: Proposition 3.1, p. 1135; proof sketch pp. 1135–1136
items.note: Use Kai Theorem 13.1 through items 35 and 51 as a precise alternative proof. Its weighted count yields item 52, stronger than infinitude modulo units. The circle-method sketch still has E4/E5. Keep these two proof routes separate: the schematic Mitsui input 33 is not a checked substitute for Kai’s theorem.

items.name: Kai's theorem on linear patterns of prime elements in number fields
items.statement: Kai v5 Theorem 13.1: let K be a number field, S a finite set of nonzero prime ideals, a a nonzero fractional ideal, and psi_1,…,psi_t:Z^d→a[S^(-1)] affine-linear maps (t,d≥1). Each linear part has torsion cokernel, and the restriction of each linear part to the kernel of any other has torsion cokernel. For A>1 and Omega⊆[−N,N]^d with boundary in Lip(d,Z,L_0 N), the weighted sum of product_i Lambda^a_(O_K[S^(-1)])(psi_i(x)) over integer x in Omega equals C_(S,Psi) Vol(Omega)/Res_(s=1)(zeta_K(s))^t + O_(K,S,Psi,Z,L_0,A)(N^d(log N)^(−A)), for sufficiently large N. C_(S,Psi) is the product over rational primes p of (p^[K:Q]/phi_K(p))^t times the proportion of classes modulo p outside all zero sets psi_i modulo primes above p outside S. It is positive when for every p there is an x for which all the ideal norms Norm(psi_i(x)a[S^(-1)]^(-1)) are prime to p. For O_K-linear source lattices this is equivalent to nonvanishing of all forms modulo each prime ideal outside S. Here phi_K(p)=#(O_K/p O_K)^×.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 1136, citing [10, Theorem 13.1]
items.note: Read pp. 56–57 of v5 independently. In our application S is empty, a=I, the lattice has Z-rank 2[F:Q], and the congruence set is an affine coset, not a subgroup (E7; item 51). Torsion-cokernel conditions are checked using beta≠0. Prime powers and residue-degree>1 primes must be discarded before concluding I-primality (item 52).

items.name: Class field theory for K/F: ray class character, splitting and conductor
items.statement: A quadratic K/F of conductor 𝔪 corresponds to a surjection ψ : Cl_F(𝔪) → ℤ/2. The primes dividing 𝔪 are exactly those ramified in K. A prime 𝔭 ∤ Disc(K/F) splits in K if and only if [𝔭] ∈ ker ψ. Restricted to Gal(H_𝔪/H) ≅ (𝒪_F/𝔪)^×/π_𝔪(𝒪_F^×), ψ has an index-2 kernel G_0 when K ⊄ H. A principal prime (p) ∤ 𝔪 is inert in K if and only if p mod 𝔪 ∉ G_0, that is, ∏_{𝔭|𝔪} χ_𝔭(p) = −1.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, pp. 1136–1137
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layers 12–13 plan the global correspondence and ray class fields. The ray class group and its map to the class group are built in Tau Ceti: `TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup`, `rayClassToClassGroup` and `card_ker_rayClassToClassGroup_mul_index`.

items.name: Chebotarev for the abelian extension HK/F
items.statement: If K ⊄ H (the Hilbert class field), there are infinitely many principal primes of F that are inert in K. Every ideal class, in particular one outside ker ψ, contains infinitely many prime ideals.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, pp. 1136–1137
items.note: Tau Ceti Chebotarev plans abelian and Dirichlet-density Chebotarev. Its audit records the construction as unfinished.

items.name: Siegel–Mahler finiteness for S-unit equations
items.statement: For a number field F, finite set T of finite primes and fixed c∈F^×, the equation x+c y=1 has finitely many solutions with x,y∈O_(F,T)^×. Enlarge T by the prime support of c and apply the S-unit theorem to x+(c y)=1. The hypothesis c≠0 is necessary: with c=0, x=1 and y varies freely.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1137
items.note: DT.2 plans S-unit equations (x + y = 1 in S-units). Its audit notes that only the S-unit group and its finite generation (`Set.unit_fg`, Tau Ceti) exist.

items.name: Units close to 1 are ℓ-th powers
items.statement: For every prime 𝔭 of F, including 𝔭 | ℓ, there is k with 1 + 𝔭^k ⊆ F_𝔭^{×ℓ}. This is used to make 1 − 2rb, γ^{nℓ} and p_2/p_3 ℓ-th powers at 𝔭 ∈ S.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1136
items.note: Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 plans `isOpen_range_powMonoidHom` with U(K, i + v(n)) ⊆ (K^×)^n in mixed characteristic. The tame case 𝔭 ∤ ℓ is built: `TauCeti.HenselianRing.exists_pow_eq_and_sub_one_mem_of_sub_one_mem`.

items.name: Local solvability of the residue conditions modulo 𝔪
items.statement: After replacing the chosen r by r′=r delta^ell, where delta is supported on dyadic primes dividing the conductor m and has sufficiently large valuation there, there are units u_1,u_2,u_3 modulo m with psi(u_i)=−1 and u_1+2r′ gamma^(n ell)u_2=u_3 modulo m. Choose t_1=t_3 and t_2 in the nontrivial character coset. At dyadic primes the middle coefficient vanishes modulo m, so x=y=z=1 works. At odd ramified primes ell is invertible, r′ and gamma are units and the residue field has q≥2ell+1≥7 elements. The smooth diagonal conic has q+1 points and at most six points on xyz=0, hence a point with all coordinates nonzero; Hensel lift it. Set u_i=t_i times the corresponding square and combine the local solutions by CRT.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1137
items.note: This is a statement for the rescaled r′. The curves and conductors, hence S and Sigma, are unchanged, and Sel_phi still vanishes. The original requirement r∉p at every ramified p is no longer true at the dyadic primes; retain it only at the odd ramified primes. Do not claim this change proves Proposition 2.5 for its originally fixed r (G3).

items.name: The Σ-unit solution (a, b) from a prime triple
items.statement: Given I-primes with p_1 + 2rγ^{nℓ}p_2 = p_3 and p_2 ≡ p_3 (mod 𝔭^n) for 𝔭 ∈ S, set a = p_1/p_3 and b = γ^{nℓ}p_2/p_3. Then a, b ∈ 𝒪_{F,Σ}^×, a + 2rb = 1, and for n large a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b is an ℓ-th power at every 𝔭 ∈ S. The ideal (a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b) equals 𝔱_{p_1,p_2,p_3}(γ^n p_3^{−1})^ℓ with 𝔱 = (p_1^{(ℓ−1)/2}p_2p_3^{(ℓ−1)/2}).
items.locator: (3.1) and the end of the proof of Proposition 2.5, pp. 1136–1137
items.note: This is the bridge from Proposition 3.1 to the set X.

items.name: Finiteness of the number-field ideal class group
items.statement: For a number field F, the ideal class group of O_F is finite, with positive class number h_F equal to its cardinality. This is the library input for the separate supported-element construction 56.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1136
items.note: The cited instance and definition have exactly this narrower scope. The extraction previously labelled the whole gamma construction as a library declaration.

items.name: Assembly of the proof of Theorem 1.1
items.statement: With ζ_ℓ ∈ F and K/F unramified above ℓ, fix r (Lemma 2.3) and (a, b) as in Proposition 2.7. Then rank J_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F) > 0, and by Lemmas 2.1 and 2.4, rank J_{q^ℓr²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F) = 0. By item 13, rank J_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(K) = rank J_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F) + rank J_{q^ℓr²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F) = rank J_{r²a^{ℓ−1}b²}(F) > 0. Remove ζ_ℓ by Weil restriction (item 12).
items.note: This is the final step of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Siegel–Mahler support argument: infinitely many ℓ-th power classes
items.statement: If a family of Σ-unit solutions (a, b) of a + 2rb = 1 has ideals (a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b) whose prime-to-𝒮 parts involve infinitely many primes with exponent ≢ 0 mod ℓ, then {a^{(ℓ−1)/2}b} meets infinitely many classes of F^×/F^{×ℓ}.
items.locator: end of the proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1137
items.note: This is the final counting step of Proposition 2.5. As printed, it relies on the multiplicity claim that fails for proportional triples (E6).

items.name: Replace finite polynomial systems by one equation
items.statement: If R is a domain and Frac(R) is not algebraically closed, any finite polynomial system over R is equivalent over R to one polynomial equation. Choose a nonconstant polynomial over R with no root in Frac(R), homogenize it to a binary form vanishing only at (0,0), and iterate on the system. The combination is effective once the root-free polynomial is fixed.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.1, p. 9; used for published Corollary 1.2

items.name: Transitivity of Diophantine definitions
items.statement: If subrings R⊆S⊆T have R Diophantine in S and S Diophantine in T, then R is Diophantine in T: constrain every witness for the first definition to S using its defining system.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.3, first clause, p. 9

items.name: Finite intersections of Diophantine sets
items.statement: A finite intersection of Diophantine subsets of R^k is Diophantine: conjoin defining systems using disjoint witness variables.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.5, p. 10; proof of Theorem 4.8

items.name: Descent through a finite extension of integer rings
items.statement: For number fields K⊆L⊆H with H/L finite, if O_K is Diophantine over O_H, it is Diophantine over O_L. Express O_H as a finite O_L-module using an integral generating set and polynomial coordinate equations; the standard finite-extension descent accounts for relations among generators.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.3, second clause, and Remark 4.4, p. 9

items.name: Denef’s definition of nonzero algebraic integers
items.statement: For any algebraic extension K/Q and x∈O_K, x≠0 iff there are y,z,w∈O_K with (2y−1)(3z−1)=xw. For x≠0 work in Q(x), split the ideal (x) into factors prime to 2 and 3, and use CRT; for x=0 either 1/2 or 1/3 would be integral.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.6 and proof, p. 10

items.name: Recover the integer ring from a Diophantine set containing N
items.statement: Let L/K be algebraic, K a number field. If S⊆O_K contains N and is Diophantine over O_L, then O_K is Diophantine over O_L. Fix an integral primitive element alpha for K; express bx as a bounded-degree polynomial in alpha with b∈S nonzero and coefficients in S−S. Every such x∈O_L belongs to K, and every element of O_K admits such an expression.
items.locator: MRS v3 Lemma 4.7, p. 10; used in Theorem 3.1’s proof

items.name: Affine lattice of admissible prime triples
items.statement: For the data of Proposition 3.1, CRT gives x_0,y_0∈I with the chosen residues. W=(x_0,y_0)+(CI)^2 is the congruence coset in I². Choose a Z-basis of I² to identify its translation lattice with Z^(2d), d=[F:Q]. The maps x,y,x+beta y become affine-linear maps to I. Their linear parts and pairwise restrictions to kernels have finite-index images because beta≠0. At p|C the prescribed residues are units; at p∤C choose nonzero x,y with x+beta y≠0 in I/pI. For residue cardinality two, beta∈2O_F removes the only obstruction. Thus Kai’s local factors are positive.
items.locator: Published proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 1136; correction E7; Kai v5 Theorem 13.1

api.name: PrimeTripleCoset.of_crt
api.statement: CRT supplies the basepoint in I² because (I,C)=1.

api.name: PrimeTripleCoset.translation

api.name: PrimeTripleCoset.local_admissible

items.name: Prime triples outside finitely many proportional families
items.statement: For the data of Proposition 3.1, there are ≫ N^(2d)/(log N)^3 I-prime triples of archimedean height at most N, d=[F:Q]. Apply item 35 on a positive-volume convex region in the affine lattice 51 with all three forms bounded by N. Prime-power and residue-degree>1 contributions are o(N^(2d)); bound their values by O(N^(d/2) polylog N) and the remaining lattice variable by O(N^d). A fixed F-proportional family contributes O(N^d), so there are infinitely many distinct ratios (p_1/p_3,p_2/p_3). Outside the fixed support of I beta, if two residual prime ideals coincide, the third coincides too; such triples have unit ratios and give only finitely many proportional families by S-unit finiteness. Remove those families. Every remaining large prime in (p_1^((ell−1)/2)p_2 p_3^((ell−1)/2)) then has exponent below ell. The infinite ratio family cannot have finite prime support by item 38.
items.locator: Independent expanded deduction of Kai v5 Theorem 13.1 for published Proposition 3.1 and the E6 repair, pp. 1135–1137
items.proofOutline: The affine lattice has rank 2d. Take the inverse image of a sufficiently small bounded convex body on which all three nonconstant forms have height at most N; its volume is cN^(2d), c>0. Kai’s product local density is positive by item 51. Choose A>4 in its error bound, then divide the weighted main term by O((log N)^3). Elements of bounded height whose residual ideal is a higher prime power or has residue degree at least two are O(N^(d/2) polylog N): count the underlying prime ideals and use the logarithmic unit lattice to bound associates in the archimedean box. A fibre of any of the three forms has O(N^d) lattice points, so discarding these values has negligible weighted contribution. Each fixed proportional line contributes O(N^d) integral pairs. For the multiplicity claim remove all triples with repeated residual primes outside I beta: the equation forces all three primes to agree, hence the ratios are units. Their unit equation has only finitely many solutions by item 38. The remaining infinitely many ratio classes have infinite support by the same S-unit theorem and all new valuations are nonzero modulo ell.

items.name: Quadratic cyclotomic base change and unramifiedness
items.statement: If K/F is quadratic and ell is an odd prime not dividing Disc(K), set F′=F(ζ_ell) and K′=K(ζ_ell). Then [K′:F′]=2, F′ is totally complex, and K′/F′ is unramified above ell. Disjointness from item 11 gives the degree by tensor base change. Unramifiedness follows because the original extension is unramified above ell and finite etale local algebras remain etale after base change, including the ramified cyclotomic base change.
items.locator: Published §4, p. 1137; separated from original item 11

items.name: A nonzero x-coordinate excludes the phi-kernel
items.statement: For the pointed smooth curve C_n of genus (ell−1)/2≥1, if an affine P has x(P)≠0 then AJ(P)∉J_n[1−ζ]. Indeed, AJ is injective on geometric points: a principal divisor P−Q for P≠Q would give a degree-one map to P¹, forcing genus zero. Equivariance gives AJ(ζP)=AJ(P) if (1−ζ)AJ(P)=0, hence ζP=P, contrary to x(P)≠0. The same argument works with the inverse action if pullback conventions are used.
items.locator: Implicit step in Proposition 2.7, p. 1135; independent proof from the divisor interpretation of Abel–Jacobi

items.name: A degree-one divisor relation forces genus zero
items.statement: If X is a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over an algebraically closed field and P≠Q with P−Q principal, the corresponding rational function has degree one and gives an isomorphism X≅P¹. Hence for genus at least one the pointed Abel map is injective on geometric points.
items.locator: Divisor/function-field input to item 54; Jacobian Challenge Layers A, B, F and Algebraic Curves
items.note: Use the divisor interpretation and Riemann–Roch from these existing layers; do not plan a second general Jacobian or reduced-divisor API.

items.name: Supported elements for S and for the dyadic rescaling
items.statement: For the paper’s finite S choose, for each p∈S, a generator gamma_p of p^h_F; gamma=product gamma_p has exactly prime support S. For the dyadic primes dividing m, choose multiples of h_F large enough to exceed the prescribed conductor valuations, and multiply generators to obtain delta with exactly that support. If the support is empty take 1. These are applications of finite class-group exponent and unique ideal factorization, not new definitions of the class group.
items.locator: Published proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 1136; E3 repair

items.name: Quadratic eigenspace rank decomposition
items.statement: For an abelian variety A/F and quadratic K/F with nontrivial sigma, A(K)⊗Q splits via (1+sigma)/2 and (1−sigma)/2. Its plus part is A(F)⊗Q by descent and its minus part is A^K(F)⊗Q by the twist isomorphism. Taking dimensions proves item 13; this is a rational decomposition, not generally an integral direct sum. The sum/difference morphism A×A^K→Res_(K/F)(A_K) is an isogeny: after K-base change it is the matrix ((1,1),(1,−1)), whose square is [2] in each factor. Its finite kernel/cokernel comparison is the geometric form of the rational eigenspace identity.
items.locator: Published §4; expanded proof of original item 13

items.name: Quadratic twist of an abelian variety
items.statement: For an abelian variety A/F and a quadratic extension K/F, descend A_K with descent datum obtained by multiplying the nontrivial Galois action by [−1]. The result A^K/F is an abelian variety, equipped with a K-isomorphism to A_K whose conjugate is its negative. Its isomorphism class is independent of the chosen presentation. Finite Galois descent of the projective variety and its group law gives the construction; the identity and a symmetric ample bundle descend (take a Galois-invariant tensor product).
items.locator: Implicit in published §§1 and 4; the general construction behind item 13
items.note: A6 owns the Weil-restriction/isogeny comparison. Its descent inputs come from A2. The elliptic quadraticTwistPointEquiv is a compatibility test, not the general construction.

routes.reason: ES.4 owns sums-of-primes theorems through a prime-weighted branch (Vaughan identity, Type I/II estimates, uniform major-arc estimates), and asks that each endpoint be a separate source theorem. ES.3 owns singular series and their positivity. Proposition 3.1 is exactly such an endpoint over a number field: three I-primes in the equation p_1 + βp_2 = p_3 with β ∈ 2𝒪_F and congruence conditions. It is Mitsui's generalization of Vinogradov and van der Corput, with a singular series made positive by the parity hypothesis on β. The layer's ℤ-case targets are absent from both libraries (audit), so the number-field version is new but squarely in its direction. The source's sketch has two formula slips (E4, E5) and needs the count to give non-proportional triples (E6). The accepted route uses the exact Kai application and the quantitative non-proportional refinement, with the lattice translation and prime-power removal explicit. The classical circle-method proof remains a separate source-acquisition obligation.

AN.4, as narrowed by RS-07, keeps the prime-ideal applications of Dedekind and Hecke L-functions. Mitsui's generalized prime number theorem (equidistribution of prime elements in ray and residue classes, with Siegel–Walfisz uniformity) is such an application, and it is the major-arc input to Proposition 3.1. The AN.4 audit records Hecke characters and their L-functions as absent.

AC.5 owns finite-complexity systems of linear equations in primes, with local factors and proportional degeneracies excluded. Kai's Theorem 13.1 is that theorem for prime elements of a number field, and the paper uses it as the alternative proof of Proposition 3.1. AC.5's audit finds no linear-equations-in-primes result in either library. Freeze the exact weighted theorem of Kai v5, pp. 56–57, not an unspecified finite-complexity slogan. The forms in this application satisfy its finite-index hypotheses.

A6 owns Weil restriction of abelian schemes along finite étale maps and the arithmetic of their Hom groups, including the induction formula for Tate modules. For quadratic K/F, Res_{K/F}(A_K) is isogenous to A × A^K, which gives rank A(K) = rank A(F) + rank A^K(F). This is the general abelian-variety statement the paper uses twice. The atlas plans only the elliptic case over ℚ (RankZeroOneBSD BSD.1), so the general statement belongs with A6's Weil restriction rather than in a consumer. Use the rational plus/minus eigenspace proof; import Mordell–Weil from RP.1, and geometric quadratic descent, rather than assuming the elliptic-only Tau Ceti point equivalence supplies it.

routes.title: Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration, Part II: Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers
routes.brief:
Start after LD.4’s negative solution of Hilbert’s tenth problem over Z. Targets, exactly as in the published paper: for every quadratic number-field extension K/F there is an abelian variety A/F with rank A(F)=rank A(K)>0 (Theorem 1.1); Z is Diophantine over O_K for every number field K and polynomial solvability over O_K is undecidable (Corollary 1.2). The stated Eisenträger consequence is undecidability over every infinite finitely generated commutative Z-algebra.

Build Diophantine subsets of arbitrary commutative rings and finite tuples with the APIs/tests in items 1 and 45–50: system reduction, transitivity, intersection, finite-extension descent, nonzero constraints and the integer-ring recovery lemma. Keep MRS Theorems 3.1 and 4.8 and Denef’s totally real case as exact external theorem inputs with their own complete source decomposition. Handle an already totally real Galois closure directly, rather than treating identity conjugation as quadratic. The MRS argument and Eisenträger’s general-ring reduction must not be replaced by an unsupported transfer of MRDP.

Construct the specific pointed curves C_n:y²=x^ell+n for n≠0, ell odd prime and mu_ell⊂F, their CM automorphism and explicit twists. Compute phi=1−ζ, its degree ell, kernel and quadratic Galois character. Derive the cyclotomic-rank Selmer bound, local silence and Yu’s rank-zero twist preserving unit conditions at ramified primes. Define S,Sigma exactly as item 24; use the existing Set.unit group even though Sigma is infinite. Compare every local condition under fixed coefficient identifications.

For the positive-rank construction use the corrected Fermat cover on y≠0, its extension to the smooth projective curves, and its explicit image of (1,1). Use a symmetric ample canonical height and Northcott on the fixed untwisted Jacobian for the finite exceptional set. Item 54 proves the non-phi-kernel condition from injectivity of Abel–Jacobi; general reduced-divisor normal forms need not be rebuilt. Import the precise prime-triple theorem with infinitely many proportional classes from ES.4 and the exact Kai theorem from AC.5; the congruence domain is an affine coset. Remove the finitely many unit-ratio families before the prime multiplicity argument.

The dyadic correction must be stated honestly. Replacing r by r delta^ell, with delta supported on dyadic ramified primes, preserves the curve and Selmer group and repairs the residue construction for that chosen r. It loses the dyadic unit condition on r and does not identify the original X with the new X. Gap G3 requires a proof for the originally fixed r in Proposition 2.5, or an explicitly proved reformulation sufficient for Theorem 1.1 while retaining that statement’s unresolved proof. G2 requires the complete Eisenträger Chapter 7 reduction, including positive characteristic and zero divisors. This route is not accepted while these obligations remain.

Import once: LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.0/LD.4 (MRDP); Jacobian Challenge Layers A,B,D–F (divisors, Riemann–Roch, Jacobian and Abel–Jacobi); Algebraic Curves Layer 10 (hyperelliptic function fields); HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.0/RP.1 (ample canonical heights, Northcott, Mordell–Weil and isogeny Selmer); Elliptic Curves Layer 7 (general discrete-module Selmer structures); Class Field Theory Layers 5,12,13 (local duality/Euler characteristic and ray-class splitting); Chebotarev Layer 10; Local Fields and Ramification Layer 1 (deep local powers); NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 (good reduction); AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3/A6 and this paper’s route 4 (finite-isogeny degrees, Weil restriction and quadratic twists/ranks); DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.2 (S-unit finiteness, nonzero coefficient); ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.3/ES.4 and AdditiveCombinatorics AC.5 (prime triples). Mitsui’s AN.4 route remains separate and requires G1; it is not needed if the exact Kai proof is used.

Acceptance tests include ell=3, the dyadic ring Z[zeta_3]/4, the old wrong Fermat formula, nonprincipal I, affine cosets that do not contain zero, higher-residue-degree primes excluded from I-primality, and the integral-versus-rational eigenspace distinction. Record Koymans–Pagano as a separate proof source for the same target, without duplicating this roadmap. Nothing is claimed formalised.
routes.reason: LD.4 plans the negative answer over ℤ and states that each other ring needs its own interpretation theorem. No layer of the atlas plans Diophantine definitions over rings of integers, the Denef and Mazur–Rubin–Shlapentokh transfer theorems, or rank stability in quadratic extensions. These are new layers in LD.4's direction, so they form a Part II of the Logic roadmap that starts at its MRDP endpoint. The arithmetic of the CM Jacobians of y² = x^ℓ + n is specific to this application: silent primes, Yu's twist, silent twists, the Σ-unit construction and the Fermat-cover points. It lives here, and every general input (Jacobians, isogeny Selmer groups, duality, class field theory, Chebotarev, Weil restriction, S-units, the three-prime theorem) is imported from its owner.
